lenders.broker_program: Not documented.
lenders.fit_notes: A large-balance bridge-to-FHA lender (e.g. $87.5M bridge on 9 SNFs; a $315M syndicated Texas seniors bridge repaid by FHA). Caveat: no dated 2025-26 seniors bridge deal was found, and most examples are 2017-2020.

lenders.name: X-Caliber Capital (X-Caliber Funding)
lenders.parent_or_aka: X-Caliber Capital Corp.; bridge platform X-Caliber Funding LLC
lenders.property_types: SNF, Assisted living, Memory care, Senior housing
lenders.programs: Bridge-to-HUD (interim until FHA permanent), Mezzanine lending program, HUD refinance (covered by other analyst)
lenders.max_leverage: Mezz program: up to 75% LTV for seniors/healthcare
lenders.term: Bridge: e.g. 3-yr. Mezz: up to 36 mo with extension options
lenders.broker_program: Not documented in search extracts.
lenders.address: 3 W. Main St, Suite 103 (city not shown in extract)
lenders.fit_notes: A bridge-to-HUD specialist with a published seniors/healthcare mezz program ($1M-$15M, up to 75% LTV; PDF updated Dec 2024). Bridge examples: a $40M 3-yr bridge on a 10-facility IL SNF/AL portfolio, and a $1.6M 3-yr bridge. The min/max loan figures refer to the mezz program. California deals not confirmed. [Research note: lender website could not be fetched (network policy); values come from search-result excerpts of the cited pages.]

lenders.name: Hudson Realty Capital (Senior Housing & Healthcare Bridge)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Hudson Realty Capital LLC (New York City)
lenders.programs: Senior housing / SNF bridge (conventional and bridge-to-HUD)
lenders.broker_program: Intermediary-arranged deal documented: Ziegler served as exclusive financial advisor on Hudson's first senior bridge loans ($37.75M, two AL/MC communities for Columbia Pacific Advisors, Oct 2021). No broker-fee policy published.
lenders.fit_notes: Launched a dedicated senior housing/SNF bridge platform in 2022 targeting $300-400M over 18-24 months. Its pipeline was about 70% AL/MC. Caveat: all sources are from 2021-22, so 2025-26 activity is unverified.

lenders.name: Love Funding (Bridge-to-HUD)
lenders.programs: Bridge-to-HUD (acquisition, lease-up, construction completion), HUD 232 (covered by other analyst)
lenders.broker_program: Not documented.
lenders.fit_notes: A HUD lender with its own bridge program of up to 3 years for borrowers headed to HUD 232. Examples range from a $2.6M Tomball TX bridge-to-HUD to a $20.1M Anchorage AK construction bridge. Caveat: deal examples are 2015-2018, and current bridge appetite is unverified.

lenders.name: Northwind Group (Northwind Healthcare Debt Fund II)
lenders.footprint: National (since 2016, 423 SNF/senior living assets across 26 states)
lenders.programs: Structured financing / mezzanine, Bridge-to-HUD loans (typically alongside senior lenders)
lenders.broker_program: Not documented.
lenders.fit_notes: Closed the $342.5M Healthcare Debt Fund II in Nov 2025, above its $250M target. Provides gap and bridge-to-HUD capital on income-producing SNF and senior housing portfolios, e.g. co-leading $105M of mezz loans with CareTrust REIT in 2024. Best for larger SNF portfolios needing subordinate capital.

lenders.name: LTC Properties (Structured Finance)
lenders.programs: Mortgage loans, Mezzanine loans, Preferred equity, Sale-leasebacks, JVs
lenders.rate_range: e.g. 8.25% fixed mortgage (Q3 2025); mezz 8% with 11-12% exit IRR (2022 example)
lenders.term: e.g. 5-yr mortgage; mezz about 5 yr + extensions
lenders.broker_program: Not documented. Lends mainly to operator relationships.
lenders.fit_notes: In Q3 2025 it originated about $58M of 5-yr fixed 8.25% mortgage loans secured by two California seniors housing communities (171 units). It still offers mezz and pref equity, though it is shifting toward SHOP and expects $265.9M of payoffs in 2026. Best for operators wanting REIT capital with a lease or purchase path.

lenders.name: CareTrust REIT (Real Estate Lending)
lenders.programs: First mortgage loans, Mezzanine loans, Preferred equity
lenders.rate_range: YE2025 weighted averages: mortgage 8.8%, mezz 12.1%, pref equity 11.5%
lenders.broker_program: Not documented. Lends to operators and owners within its relationship network.
lenders.fit_notes: About $881M of real estate loans and investments at YE2025 (mortgage $740M, mezz $57M, pref $84M), including a $30M preferred equity investment in an SNF owner at 12% (Jun 2025). A gap-capital source for larger SNF/AL operators, not small brokered deals.

lenders.name: Omega Healthcare Investors (Operator Loans)
lenders.programs: Mortgage loans, Mezzanine loans (secured by leasehold mortgages / equity pledges / 2nd liens), Non-real-estate operator loans
lenders.broker_program: Not documented. Loans go to existing or new Omega operators.
lenders.fit_notes: Makes mortgage and mezz loans to its operators: $68M mezz in 2023 for a 13-facility WV acquisition, and $8.7M mezz plus a $29.5M mortgage on 2 PA facilities. Also held 40 non-real-estate loans to 27 borrowers at YE2025. Relevant only for operators entering an Omega relationship.

lenders.name: Sabra Health Care REIT (Loans Receivable)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Sabra Health Care REIT, Inc. (Nasdaq: SBRA)
lenders.programs: Mortgage loans, Other operator loans
lenders.broker_program: Not documented. Legacy loans to operators and tenants.
lenders.fit_notes: Loan book of about $442M at YE2025, mostly three SNF/behavioral mortgage loans. No mezzanine program found, and the 'Other' loan balance shrank during 2025. Minimal relevance as a broker-channel lender.

lenders.name: Kayne Anderson Real Estate Debt (KARED IV)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Kayne Anderson Real Estate (Kayne Anderson Capital Advisors)
lenders.footprint: National (senior housing investments in 110+ communities across 25 states since 2013)
lenders.property_types: Senior living, Medical office, Other specialized housing
lenders.programs: Real estate debt (fourth flagship debt fund, KARED IV)
lenders.broker_program: Not documented.
lenders.fit_notes: Closed the $1.875B KARED IV debt fund in Jul 2026, explicitly targeting senior living among other sectors. The firm is also a major senior housing equity owner. Caveat: no specific 2025-26 senior housing loan by the debt arm was found, so appetite and loan size are unconfirmed.
